newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy opposition set to win Milan but lose Trieste.
newsitem.headline: Italy opposition set to win Milan but lose Trieste.

text.p: Italy's centre-right opposition bloc was poised to win the mayoral race in the prize industrial city of Milan, but looked set to lose in two other key northern cities, early results from Sunday's local elections showed.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's ruling centre-left Olive Tree coalition was on course for a clear victory in the north-eastern centre of Trieste and was also marginally ahead in another northern Italian powerhouse, Turin.

Some 5.43 million Italians were eligible to vote in Sunday's elections for 77 mayors and five provincial presidents between the two front runners in places where no-one gained more than 50 percent support in first round voting on April 27.

Former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Freedom Alliance opposition bloc was hoping to use Sunday's contests to relaunch its lagging fortunes after suffering a surprise defeat in a general election last year.

Projections based on early results from Italy's second city, Milan, showed Freedom Alliance candidate, industrialist Gabriele Albertini, securing 53.1 percent of the vote while his rival Aldo Fumagalli took 46.9 percent.

The separatist Northern League party had controlled Italy's financial capital for the past four years, but outgoing mayor Marco Formentini was easily beaten into third place in the first round ballot.

In neighbouring Turin, home of car giant Fiat, centre-left candidate Valentino Castellani was slightly ahead with 51.1 percent against 48.9 percent for the centre-right's Raffaele Costa after almost half the votes had been counted.
In Trieste, Riccardo Illy of the centre-left seemed certain to cruise home with 53.8 percent against 46.2 percent for his rival after two thirds of the vote had been counted.

The races in the troika of wealthy north Italian cities were the most closely watched in the entire run-off contest, with particular interest focused on relations between the hard-left Communist Refoundation and Olive Tree candidates.

In Milan and Trieste, the centre-left coalition representatives refused to sign electoral pacts with Refoundation, despite the fact that the hardline party secures Prodi's majority in the lower house of parliament.
However Castellani in Turin joined forces with Refoundation to boost his election chances.
Corriere della Sera newspaper said on Sunday the centre-right opposition would get a perverse boost if the Olive Tree lost Milan but took Turin.
"It would be proof that the Olive Tree is ever-more dependent on the neo-Communists," it said in an editorial.
Television polls showed that the centre-right was on course for clear cut wins in the southern cities of Catanzaro and Crotone as well as in the central city of Terni.
By contrast, the Olive Tree was ahead in the northern city of Novara and in the southern city of Ancona.
The separatist Northern League party, which did disastrously in the first round ballot, made a stronger showing on Sunday.

In the only two cities where its candidates won through to the second round run-offs, Pordenone and Lecco, League candidates were leading in both races against centre-left opponents, initial projections said.
